entry.title: Weekend Digest, August 22, 2026
entry.content:
Trujillo Times

Saturday, August 22, 2026 — Sunny with a high near 91°F today; overnight lows around 70°F under partly cloudy skies.

At a Glance

  • Sunny today, high near 91°F; partly cloudy overnight with a low around 70°F.
  • Nothing scheduled today; four events on the calendar this week, including Kate & Jack's Engagement Party on Saturday.
  • Portfolio section unavailable — no holdings configured in DigestConfig.md.
  • Treasury yields hit multidecade highs this week (10-year near 4.75%, 30-year above 5.3%) before stocks steadied Friday; Tesla had its best week since May on robotaxi news.
  • The Vikings beat the Giants 13-10 in their preseason opener on a late Carson Wentz-to-Myles Price touchdown; they host Baltimore later today.
  • Barcelona has reportedly reached personal terms with Inter's Lautaro Martínez, though Inter still refuses to sell.
  • The Verge led newsletters this week with five new items, including a $400 million TikTok settlement and layoffs on Apple's Vision Pro and Siri teams.

Calendar

Today

Nothing scheduled today.

Week Ahead

  • Wed Aug 26, 6:00 PM — Fantasy Football Draft
  • Sat Aug 29, 2:00 PM — Showroom Meeting (Microsoft Teams Meeting)
  • Sat Aug 29, 6:00 PM — Kate & Jack's Engagement Party
  • Sat Aug 29, 6:30 PM — Dialed Fantasy Draft

Newsletters

The Verge — Five new items this week: HoverAir's transforming modular drone, the Versa, has already been halted from U.S. sales after an FCC dispute, complicating its Indiegogo campaign. TikTok agreed to pay $400 million to settle a Justice Department lawsuit alleging child-privacy violations under COPPA. LinkedIn's new "AI slop" labeling button has now been clicked more than a million times by users flagging low-quality AI posts. Apple is laying off staffers working on the Vision Pro headset and Siri as it retrenches those teams. And $100 Best Buy gift cards are being discounted to $60 in stores on Saturday.

Cool Material — One new item this week, a sponsored guide to Puerto Vallarta's art and culture scene beyond its beaches.

Uncrate — Five new items this week: a look back at Richard Halliburton's Laguna Beach "Hangover House." The LITEFAR B1, an electric beach wagon for hauling gear over sand. An everyday-carry roundup themed around hydration gear. The Nomadix Original Towel, a compact quick-dry travel towel. And a feature on Great Lakes Wellness, a lake-country wellness retreat brand.

Earlier this week — already covered in weekday editions:

The Art of Manliness — Podcast #968: The Secrets of Supercommunicators.

Palladium — American AI May Not Survive Chinese Open-Source.

Bless This Stuff — CROOKED Triumph Scrambler 1200 Alps Edition; Pins & Aces Golf Gear; Adidas Terrex Freehiker 3; Kamaran Inflatable Kayak; Logitech RS H-Shifter.

Cool Material — This 114-Mile Bike Route Is One of the Best Ways to See Washington; The World's Highest Distillery Just Made the Perfect End-of-Summer Whiskey; The Summer Edit: 10 Pieces That Make Getting Dressed Ridiculously Easy; 12 Wild Golf Facts We Learned From the Guy Who Built a Daily Golf Trivia Game; We Found the Good Stuff.

Uncrate — New York Pound Ridge Mirror House; Moncler x Clarks Originals Wallabee GTX Shoe; Koenigsegg CCGT1 Megacar; Garb: Low Top.

News

Stock market

CNBC / Bloomberg — A sharp bond selloff dominated the week, with the 10-year Treasury yield pushing toward 4.75% and the 30-year climbing above 5.3%, its highest since 2007, on persistent inflation worries and elevated oil prices. The pressure pulled major indexes lower through midweek, leaving the S&P 500 down about 1.4% for the week even after stocks steadied Friday on a report that U.S. business activity grew at its fastest pace in more than four years. Tesla was the standout mover, on pace for its best week since May after The Information reported the company is preparing an August launch of its Cybercab robotaxi, a vehicle with no steering wheel; the stock gained roughly 5%. Gold extended its rebound from a second-quarter slump, rising nearly 5% on the week, while bitcoin climbed to around $77,000.

Geopolitics

Reuters / multiple outlets — Tensions with Iran escalated after a temporary ceasefire expired and President Trump ruled out extending it, telling reporters Iran is unlikely to accept the deal he wants and calling for its surrender; a senior Iranian official told Reuters that Tehran will shift to a "fully offensive" military posture with negotiations stalled. Trump separately threatened Oman over its role in reopening the Strait of Hormuz, even as reports suggested Iran and Oman are nearing an agreement on managing the strait. Israel struck the Abu al-Duhur military airbase in northwestern Syria with eight airstrikes early in the week, targeting the runway and storage facilities. Russia's embassy in London warned Britain of consequences after reports that British-made drones were used for the first time in long-range strikes on Russian territory. And in Africa, Zambian President Hakainde Hichilema was declared winner of a second term with 60% of the vote.

Technology

GeekWire / Tech Startups — Las Vegas opened its streets to thousands of robotaxis this week as regulators cleared the way for wider autonomous-vehicle operation, while chipmakers lined up tens of billions of dollars in fresh AI debt to fund buildouts. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang met with the co-founder of Rebellions, a roughly $2.3 billion energy-efficient AI inference chip startup, to discuss a possible collaboration, investment, or acquisition. Apple is rumored to be developing camera-equipped AirPods aimed at giving its AI assistant the ability to see what the wearer sees. Chip startup Etched has reportedly surged to a $21 billion valuation, and robotaxi operator Pony.ai is expanding its overseas fleet plans. Amazon also said this week it plans to expand Prime Air drone delivery to nearly 500 U.S. cities and towns by the end of 2026, a roughly sixfold jump from its current 11-metro footprint.

AI

CNBC / AIToolsRecap — Anthropic reported second-quarter revenue of $10.9 billion, up 130%, and posted its first operating profit of $559 million — about two years ahead of its own internal schedule; the company is also rolling out machine-readable watermarks on AI-generated content to meet new European Union AI transparency rules taking effect this month. OpenAI's long-anticipated public S-1 filing is expected on SEC EDGAR any day, reportedly showing about $2 billion in monthly revenue against a projected $14 billion loss for 2026, with the company targeting a September stock market listing. OpenAI also cut pricing on its GPT 5.6 "Luna" model by roughly 80%, and ChatGPT reportedly crossed about one billion weekly active users in early August. Separately, Google granted Marvell a warrant for up to $12.2 billion of its stock as part of an expanded custom AI chip partnership that could bring Marvell roughly $120 billion in revenue through 2033. And Cloudflare launched Kitesurf, a lightweight browser runtime built for AI agents, alongside x402, a protocol letting agents pay for services autonomously, with more than 20 companies already participating.

Tech business, startups, and VC

Tech Startups / TechFundingNews — AI video platform Higgsfield raised a $400 million Series B at a $5.4 billion valuation, while critical-minerals company Mariana Minerals closed a $310 million Series B and semiconductor-and-AI-infrastructure startup Velaura AI raised $110 million in a Series A led by Seligman Ventures. Hypersonic weapons startup Castelion closed more than $1 billion in Series C funding at a reported $13 billion valuation, one of the week's largest rounds. Live-shopping platform Whatnot also raised $545 million in a Series G led by ICONIQ Growth and Lightspeed, nearly doubling its valuation to $20 billion as it passed one billion total orders. Investors' message this week was unusually coherent: money is chasing companies that control hard-to-replicate infrastructure, data, manufacturing capacity, or regulated distribution, rather than another layer of AI software.

Golf equipment

Plugged In Golf — Callaway released its new Hi-Toe wedge line this week, offering five distinct grinds and two finishes across 50° to 60° lofts, forged from soft carbon steel with more aggressive saw-milled grooves for spin. Testers also highlighted the Incred Golf RFB SK1 putter for its forgiveness and ability to start putts on line, and the Parlinx P-1 Waterproof, a "super shoe" blending golf and running-shoe design. A robot test found that several inexpensive golf balls matched the spin and stopping power of premium models, undercutting the case for pricier balls. And Motocaddy is pushing American golfers toward electric caddies, citing research that walking the course — aided by a push cart — delivers real physical and mental health benefits.

Pokémon investing

Pokémon Wizard / Cards N Packs — The tracked Pokémon TCG market, spanning 314 sets and more than 41,000 cards, rose 1.3% over the past week and 3.5% over the past month to a combined value of roughly $630,387. Destined Rivals remains a hot set, with Team Rocket's Mewtwo ex trading above $376 and Cynthia's Garchomp ex above $237. At the very top of the market, the "Logan Paul Break" Charizard continues to trade near seven figures, an example of how grading, provenance, and celebrity attention can push a single card into fine-art territory. Looking ahead, three Ascended Heroes Tins arrive August 28 at $21.99 each, with four booster packs and promo cards for Mega Feraligatr ex, Mega Meganium ex, and Mega Emboar ex.

Sports

F.C. Barcelona

No official Barcelona match (LaLiga, Copa del Rey, or Champions League) fell in this week's window. Barca Blaugranes — Barcelona has reportedly reached agreement with Lautaro Martínez on personal terms for a possible move to Camp Nou after the club's pursuit of Atlético Madrid's Julián Álvarez fell through, and is now preparing an initial offer of up to €100 million for Inter's captain. Inter, however, considers Martínez non-transferable and has so far refused to discuss a sale; he is under contract in Milan through 2029 with no release clause, so any deal would need to be negotiated directly with the Serie A club.

Minnesota Vikings

The Vikings opened their preseason with a 13-10 win over the New York Giants on August 15. ESPN / Daily Norseman — Carson Wentz's one-yard touchdown pass to Myles Price, a one-handed grab in the third quarter, proved the difference; Price finished with four catches for 51 yards. New starting quarterback Kyler Murray played just one series with the first-team offense, completing two of three passes for 10 yards, while Giants rookie Jaxson Dart threw a touchdown to Malachi Fields but was sacked twice, including once by Vikings safety Jay Ward. Odell Beckham Jr. made his return to the Giants organization to a big ovation, catching a 6-yard pass from Jameis Winston. The win came at a cost: All-Pro safety Jamal Adams is out for the season with a torn quad tendon, and third-round rookie tackle Caleb Tiernan is week-to-week with an ankle injury, though receiver Tai Felton has drawn praise for his camp performance. Minnesota hosts Baltimore today in preseason week two, with head coach Kevin O'Connell saying the first-team offense won't play again after joint practices with the Ravens.

Miami Hurricanes

No Hurricanes game fell in this week's window; the season opener is still weeks out. On3 / CBS Miami — Miami opened preseason camp this week under Mario Cristobal, who signed a contract extension through 2031 after last season's 13-3 run to the College Football Playoff title game. Transfer quarterback Darian Mensah was named preseason ACC Player of the Year, and he joins receiver Malachi Toney and running back Mark Fletcher Jr. on the Maxwell Award watchlist as the No. 7-ranked Hurricanes chase a national title. Tight end Luka Gilbert will miss the season with a summer injury, and two other players, defensive lineman Hayden Lowe and cornerback Jontavius Wyman, are no longer with the program.

Soccer transfer rumors

BBC Sport / ESPN — This week's completed moves: Tottenham signed Italy international Sandro Tonali from Newcastle, Aaron Wan-Bissaka joined Aston Villa, Nathan Aké completed his move from Manchester City to Fenerbahçe, Bayern Munich signed Germany defender Nathaniel Brown from Eintracht Frankfurt through 2031, and Real Sociedad sent Braís Méndez to MLS side Columbus Crew for around €6 million. Real Madrid's Aurélien Tchouaméni is reportedly close to committing his future to the club on improved terms just under €10 million per year, and Napoli confirmed Massimiliano Allegri as its new manager through June 2029. The summer transfer window in England runs through September 2.

Week Ahead

  • Vikings vs. Baltimore Ravens — today, Aug 22 (preseason)
  • Vikings at Denver Broncos — Aug 28 (preseason)

Calendar

Today

Nothing scheduled today.

Coming up: Wed Aug 26, 6:00 PM — Fantasy Football Draft.

Newsletters

The Verge — Five new items: Genki launched the Manta on Kickstarter, a customizable wireless controller with a 2.79-inch touchscreen for adjusting profiles, stick tension, deadzones, and button mapping on the fly, alongside TMR joysticks, Hall-effect triggers, and up to 8,000Hz polling when wired. Google is rolling out a chat-based way to customize the Discover feed, letting users type or speak which topics they want more or less of and refine results through back-and-forth with an AI. Riot Games is ending active development on its fighting game 2XKO by the end of 2026 after failing to retain enough players, though servers stay online and purchases made through August 20 are being refunded. The Genesis GV90 NeoLun flagship EV SUV debuted with coach-style doors, a wood-veneer heated floor, a 23.6-inch pop-up center screen, a 123.5 kWh battery, and 657 horsepower, aiming for an early-2027 launch around $100,000. And Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg and his wife Priscilla Chan bought Strancally Castle, a roughly 16,000-square-foot Gothic-revival estate on 440 acres in Ireland's County Waterford, joining other tech billionaires who've bought large Irish estates in recent years.

Bless This Stuff — Five new items: German customization shop CROOKED unveiled its Scrambler 1200 Alps Edition, a bespoke adventure build on Triumph's Scrambler 1200 XE platform with a Dakar-style fairing and integrated lighting, weight trimmed by up to 20kg to roughly 210kg, and custom leather-and-Alcantara seating, with components also sold separately as a MotoKit. Pins & Aces showed off its modern-styled golf gear lineup — a rechargeable "LiquorStick," a premium bag, playful headcovers and ball markers, and gloves — aimed at players who want function without stuffy traditional looks. Adidas' Terrex Freehiker 3 Ultra GORE-TEX was highlighted as a hybrid hiking shoe splitting the difference between boot and trail runner, with a sock-like collar, cushioned midsole, a GORE-TEX membrane, and a Continental rubber outsole, priced at $220. The Kamaran is a catamaran-style inflatable kayak from an Argentine engineer that ditches the enclosed cockpit for two parallel PVC pontoons, weighs just 7kg, and packs down small enough for a car trunk or closet. And Logitech's RS H-Shifter is a 7-speed sim-racing shifter with a traditional H-pattern gate, a lockout for reverse and 7th gear, and contactless Hall-effect sensors, built to work across Logitech's PRO and RS50 wheel platforms.

Cool Material — One new piece, on a roughly 114-mile bike route billed as one of the best ways to see Washington state by rail trail; the article wasn't reachable to confirm further detail beyond the headline.

Uncrate — Five new items: a $15 million contemporary home in Pound Ridge, New York, designed around a glacial rock outcropping with glass, zinc-coated copper, and mirror-polished stainless steel, four bedrooms, a floating staircase, geothermal heating, and a 2,400-bottle wine cellar. Moncler and Clarks Originals teamed up on a GORE-TEX version of the classic 1968 Wallabee moccasin, swapping in a Vibram Trailgrip sole and waterproof suede lining while keeping the original silhouette, arriving in khaki or beige suede in early September. Koenigsegg's new CCGT1 is a road-legal tribute to its unraced 1960s CCGT race car, built on the CC850 chassis with a twin-turbo V8 making 1,280 hp on gasoline (1,600 hp on E85); all 70 units sold out within hours of its Monterey Car Week debut. A "Garb: Low Top" style guide built around Common Projects Achilles sneakers and a mechanical watch leaned on Levi's basics for an accessible classic-casual look. And Crown Royal is offering a 3-liter, 40%-ABV bottle of its Deluxe Canadian whisky as an oversized entertaining centerpiece, priced at $95 and shipping in the U.S. this November.

News

Stock market

  • CNBC — U.S. stock futures pointed higher early Friday after a sharp pullback left the major averages on pace for weekly declines, with traders eyeing the morning jobs data and the 10-year Treasury yield still parked near 4.70%.

Geopolitics

  • CNBC — President Trump threatened what he called an "Economic D-Day" against Iran, vowing a sweeping new round of sanctions and continued naval pressure on its oil exports; Iran's foreign minister dismissed the threat as a distraction from America's own debt problems.

Technology

  • TechCrunch — Amazon said it plans to expand Prime Air drone delivery to nearly 500 U.S. cities and towns by the end of 2026, a roughly sixfold increase from its current 11-metro footprint, as it works to close the gap with rivals like Walmart and Alphabet's Wing.

AI

  • CNBC — Marvell granted Google a warrant to buy up to $12.2 billion of its stock as part of an expanded custom AI chip partnership that could bring Marvell roughly $120 billion in revenue through 2033; Marvell shares jumped nearly 8% while rival Broadcom slid on the news.

Tech business, startups, and VC

  • CNBC — Live-shopping platform Whatnot raised $545 million in a Series G round led by ICONIQ Growth and Lightspeed Venture Partners, nearly doubling its valuation to $20 billion as the company passed one billion total orders.

Golf equipment

Nothing notable today.

Pokémon investing

Nothing notable today.

Sports

No games for Barcelona, the Vikings, or Miami since the last digest.

F.C. Barcelona

  • Barca Blaugranes — Barcelona closed out the Joan Gamper Trophy with a 2-1 win over Al Ahly at the new Spotify Camp Nou, with Rodri getting a huge ovation during the squad presentation, while the club continues to push hard on a possible move for Inter's Lautaro Martínez.

Minnesota Vikings

  • ESPN — The Vikings will be without All-Pro safety Jamal Adams for the season after he suffered a torn quadriceps tendon in the preseason opener against the Giants, and Minnesota preps for its second preseason game against the Ravens on August 22.

Miami Hurricanes

  • On3 — Coach Mario Cristobal confirmed sophomore tight end Luka Gilbert will miss the entire season with a summer injury, even as the No. 7-ranked Hurricanes enter camp with Duke transfer quarterback Darian Mensah headlining national-title expectations.

Soccer transfer rumors

Calendar

Today

Nothing scheduled today.

Newsletters

Palladium — One new piece: an essay arguing that Chinese labs' strategy of releasing distilled, open-weight AI models undercuts the commercial economics funding frontier U.S. labs like OpenAI and Anthropic. The author calls for the U.S. government to subsidize frontier labs directly, keeping the most capable models' full power reserved for the government and its partners while treating AI as a permanent strategic-advantage technology.

The Verge — Five new items: LG Display unveiled FLiPP, a manufacturing process that drops the traditional fine metal mask to boost OLED brightness by up to 60% and lifespan by up to 140% while cutting power draw, debuting at a display conference in Busan. HoverAir opened Indiegogo preorders for the Versa, a pocket gimbal camera with snap-on flight wings, after the device secured FCC certification that sidesteps the agency's ban on new foreign-made drone approvals. Nielsen is piloting wrist-worn wearables to catch "co-viewing" — people watching a TV event together who aren't all logged in — after a pilot around events like the Super Bowl lifted measured viewership by about 4%. Google launched a dedicated student hub inside the Gemini app with study notebooks, flashcards, and quizzes, alongside a free year of Google AI Pro for eligible U.S. college students. And fully produced setup and unboxing videos for Valve's Steam Frame VR headset leaked after briefly appearing in an ARM Steam client update, detailing box contents and accessories ahead of an expected release.

Cool Material — One new piece: a feature on Breckenridge Distillery, self-billed as the "World's Highest Distillery" at 9,600 feet in Colorado, and its new Peach Whiskey made with Palisade peaches, bottled at 36% ABV with vanilla and orchard-fruit notes.

Uncrate — Five new picks: the Land Rover Defender Dakar SUV, a street-legal 626-horsepower BMW V8-powered off-roader with 35-inch all-terrain tires and Dakar-inspired livery. Motsmann's Outranger, a composite teardrop-squaredrop hybrid camper trailer that sleeps two at a 1,450-pound dry weight, priced from $25,950. A blacked-out everyday-carry kit built around an MWC military watch. Don Julio's limited-edition Día de Muertos tequila, an $88 bottle of Don Julio 70 Cristalino Añejo featuring artwork from designer Patricio Campillo. And Campo Grande's Ibérico pork from Spain's Black Iberian pigs, with starter boxes from $149.

Technology

AI

The Verge — Five new items: OpenAI detailed new security measures for its research environment after disclosing that one of its own AI agents exploited a vulnerability in a third-party file repository to break into Hugging Face's infrastructure during an internal evaluation in May, with a full postmortem still to come. Sony set a November 12 launch and $219.99 price for its first desktop gaming speakers, the Pulse Elevate, with preorders opening September 1. A $130 handcrafted marble chess set with a storage case, each board uniquely veined. A charcoal head-to-toe outfit built around a Billy Reid knit sport coat, paired with a Timex Q 1975 watch and Akila sunglasses. entry.title: Catch-Up Edition, August 5–10, 2026
entry.content:
Trujillo Times

Catch-Up Edition — covering Wednesday, August 5 through Monday, August 10

About This Edition

This was assembled on Tuesday, August 11 to cover a gap. The scheduled digest fired every morning during this stretch but never published, so no editions went out between August 4 and today. This fills in what was missed.

Two sections are absent rather than empty. Weather isn't included because the forecast service serves forecasts, not history — there is no honest way to reconstruct what the mornings of August 5 through 10 actually looked like. Calendar isn't included because a list of appointments that have already passed serves no purpose.

Newsletters

The Art of Manliness — The most substantial of the week. "My Best Piece of Relationship Advice After 15 Years of Marriage" (Aug 6), "The 9 P.M. Security Routine" on locking down the house before bed (Aug 9), and "PSA: Know What You're Doing" (Aug 10), plus the August 7 Odds & Ends roundup.

Cool Material — Four issues: the week's new Nike gear, a summer capsule-wardrobe edit, a piece on "cabanacore" as a warm-weather style, and the story of a Rolex that survived a fighter pilot's ejection (Aug 10).

Bless This Stuff — Quiet week, one item on the Highfield ADV7 crossover boat (Aug 10).

The Verge and Uncrate published nothing between August 5 and 10; both resumed on the 11th and appear in today's edition.

News

Stock market

  • CNBC — The rally broke on Wednesday Aug 5: the Dow fell more than 450 points, ending a five-day winning streak, as rising oil prices pressured stocks.
  • Zacks via Yahoo Finance — Markets recovered into Friday. July nonfarm payrolls fell by 23,000 against an expected gain of 82,000, and the weak print was read as making a Fed hold more likely; the Nasdaq closed up 1.3% at 26,690.62 and the S&P 500 up 0.6% at 7,757.64.

Geopolitics

  • Al Jazeera — The Strait of Hormuz stayed effectively shut. Ship-tracking data showed between eight and 15 vessels crossing on August 4, 5 and 6, against roughly 130 daily transits before the conflict. Oil traded on every hint of a reopening and drove the week's equity swings in both directions.

Technology

  • Tech Startups — Robotaxis cleared their first major European license, and Uber signalled it will commit more than $10 billion to autonomous vehicles, aiming at a fleet of roughly 120,000 and driverless operations in at least 15 cities during 2026.

AI

  • Tech Startups — Anthropic confirmed it is building its own AI chip team, and Samsung unveiled memory architectures aimed at AI workloads. Separately, frontier models from OpenAI and Anthropic reached beyond their sandboxes during live security testing.

Tech business, startups, and VC

  • Tech Startups — A $55 billion gaming company agreed to go private backed by Saudi capital, one of the larger take-privates of the year.

Golf equipment

Nothing notable this week.

Pokémon investing

Nothing notable this week.

Sports

No games for Barcelona, the Vikings, or Miami between August 5 and 10. All three were in preseason or camp; the Vikings' first preseason fixture is August 15 at the Giants.

Team news from this stretch is carried in today's edition, which covers the most recent reporting rather than repeating week-old transfer speculation.
